facts.title: Making air on Mars
facts.text: Perseverance's MOXIE experiment made oxygen out of the thin Mars air, which is mostly carbon dioxide.

facts.title: Dust is dangerous
facts.text: In 2018 a dust storm covered the whole planet. It blocked the sunlight that powered the Opportunity rover, and its mission ended.

facts.title: Messages take time
facts.text: A radio signal takes about 4 to 24 minutes to travel between Earth and Mars, depending on where the planets are.

facts.title: Soil as a shield
facts.text: Piling Mars soil (regolith) over a habitat is one idea for blocking radiation. Thick, heavy material stops particles.

facts.title: Radiation at Gale
facts.text: Curiosity's RAD instrument measures radiation right here at Gale crater. On an average sol it is about 0.64 millisieverts, roughly 6 chest X-rays.

facts.title: Recycling water
facts.text: The International Space Station recycles about 98 percent of its water, including sweat and breath.

facts.title: A Mars day
facts.text: A Mars day, called a sol, is 24 hours and 39 minutes long. A Mars year is 687 Earth days.

facts.title: Flares and particles
facts.text: A solar flare is mostly light and X-rays. The particles that give astronauts a dose come from SEP events, which often follow big flares and CMEs.
